input_signals.name: Liquidity-Stressed Acquisition Spend
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(lct, act), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquisition outlays are more likely to destroy value when made by firms with weak liquidity and poor operating cash generation.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the double-counted intangible/goodwill construction with direct acquisition spending, treating unreported acquisition outlays as zero because no reported acquisition activity is economically close to no acquisition investment. The distress leg emphasizes near-term liquidity strain and internal cash-flow weakness rather than a generic Ohlson-style leverage/retained-earnings composite.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( aqc, 0 ), at ) ), sumrank( ratio( lct, act ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Flow-Strained Capex Acceleration
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(capx, at))), SUMRANK(RATIO(lct, act), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accelerating capital expenditure is a negative signal when firms lack liquidity and operating cash flow to fund that investment internally.
input_signals.reasoning: The revised sign logic is aligned: high values identify aggressive incremental capex precisely in financially strained firms, where the expected return effect should be negative. Using capex acceleration rather than low capex discipline avoids a positive-sign product being dominated by the negative main effect of distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( accel( ratio( capx, at ) ) ), sumrank( ratio( lct, act ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Demand-Mismatched Capacity Build
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(ppent, sale), 1)), SUMRANK(RATIO(lct, act), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Growth in physical capacity relative to sales is especially negative when firms face liquidity pressure and weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts from raw capex growth to a capacity-versus-demand mismatch: PP&E rising faster than sales suggests underutilized or premature expansion. When paired with current-liability pressure and poor cash generation, the expansion is more likely to become a fixed-cost burden than a productive investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( growth( ratio( ppent, sale ), 1 ) ), sumrank( ratio( lct, act ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Financed Loss Acquisition
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at), 1)), SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1), NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquisition spending predicts lower returns when it is associated with rising debt intensity and weak accumulated profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts the mechanism away from short-term working-capital stress and toward distressed deal financing: acquisitions by firms with retained-earnings deficits and increasing leverage are more likely to be risky roll-ups or value-destroying attempts to buy growth. Using the acquisition level rather than its one-year delta avoids overemphasizing noise in a lumpy, mostly-zero variable, while winsorization limits extreme deal-size influence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( ratio( coalesce( aqc, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), sumrank( delta( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 1 ), neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Acquisition During Asset Runoff
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at), 1)), SUMRANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(act, at), 1)), NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquisition spending predicts lower returns when firms are drawing down current-asset buffers and have weak accumulated profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the prior maturity-wall reshuffle by moving away from dlc/act, lct/act, sales decline, and operating cash flow. The mechanism is distressed external expansion while liquid operating buffers are shrinking, which may indicate a roll-up or turnaround gamble rather than a well-funded strategic acquisition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( ratio( coalesce( aqc, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), sumrank( neg( delta( ratio( act, at ), 1 ) ), neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Distressed Asset Renewal Surge
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1), 1)), SUMRANK(RATIO(lct, act), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A sharp increase in the net-to-gross PPE ratio predicts lower returns when firms face liquidity pressure and weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the capacity-versus-sales construction with an asset-renewal mechanism that is not algebraically tied to PP&E-to-sales growth. Distressed firms rapidly refreshing or replacing fixed assets may be forced into costly catch-up investment before their cash-flow base can support it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( delta( ratio( ppent, ppegt ), 1 ), 1 ) ), sumrank( ratio( lct, act ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Distressed Inorganic Substitution
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(capx, at)), 1))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at)), RATIO(lct, act)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquisition spending predicts lower returns when distressed firms are buying growth while underinvesting organically.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids subtracting operating cash flow from a mostly zero acquisition variable, so non-acquirers do not mechanically become high negative-cash-flow observations. The mechanism is a distressed substitution from organic capex toward acquisitions, which may indicate roll-up behavior, desperation growth, or poor capital allocation under accumulated losses and liquidity pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( rank( winsor( ratio( coalesce( aqc, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( capx, at ) ), 1 ) ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ), ratio( lct, act ) ) )

input_signals.name: Renewal Funding Shortfall
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(capx, at), RATIO(oancf, at)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Asset-renewal surges predict lower returns when capital spending exceeds operating cash generation.
input_signals.reasoning: The asset-renewal channel showed promising joint evidence, and this version conditions renewal on an internal funding shortfall rather than on a generic liquidity composite. A firm refreshing its asset base while capex outstrips cash generation may be forced into costly financing or continuation of low-return replacement projects.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( delta( ratio( ppent, ppegt ), 1 ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( sub( ratio( capx, at ), ratio( oancf, at ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Soft-Asset Rollover Fragility
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at), 1)), SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, lt), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Heavy non-goodwill intangible asset intensity predicts lower returns when firms face short-term debt rollover pressure and weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a collateral-quality mechanism rather than a cosmetic variant of non-goodwill intangible growth. Non-goodwill intangible assets may be difficult to pledge or liquidate, so firms with soft-asset-heavy balance sheets and near-term financing pressure are more vulnerable to costly refinancing or impairment risk.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( coalesce( intan, 0 ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), sumrank( ratio( dlc, lt ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Failed Prior Capex Payoff
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(capx, at), 1), 1)), SUMRANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(sale, at), 1)), NEG(RATIO(pi, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Prior high capital spending predicts lower returns when subsequent sales productivity deteriorates and pretax profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids multiplying two capex-increasing legs and instead asks whether last period’s investment failed to produce operating payoff. High prior capex is most concerning when asset turnover and profits worsen afterward, consistent with overinvestment or value-destroying continuation projects.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( lag( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ), 1 ) ), sumrank( neg( delta( ratio( sale, at ), 1 ) ), neg( ratio( pi, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Debt Rescue Over Investment
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, at), 1), ADD(RATIO(capx, at), RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at))), 1)), SUMRANK(RATIO(lct, act), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Short-term debt increases in excess of real investment outlays predict lower returns when firms already face liquidity and cash-flow stress.
input_signals.reasoning: This separates emergency balance-sheet financing from borrowing used to fund observable capex or acquisitions. In distressed firms, rising short-term debt not matched by real investment is more likely to represent liquidity plugging, rollover pressure, or rescue financing than productive expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( sub( delta( ratio( dlc, at ), 1 ), add( ratio( capx, at ), ratio( coalesce( aqc, 0 ), at ) ) ), 1 ) ), sumrank( ratio( lct, act ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Renewal Payoff Failure
input_signals.hypothesis: Prior asset-renewal surges predict lower returns when sales productivity subsequently deteriorates and operating cash flow is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the contradictory declining-net/gross leg and instead tests whether previously renewed assets are failing to produce operating payoff. The distress condition is not merely the same liquidity composite; it captures ex post demand and cash-flow failure after the renewal decision, consistent with value-destroying replacement or expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( lag( delta( ratio( ppent, ppegt ), 1 ), 1 ), 1 ) ), sumrank( neg( delta( ratio( sale, at ), 1 ) ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Acquisition Cash-Drain Aftermath
input_signals.hypothesis: Prior acquisition spending predicts lower returns when it is followed by cash depletion and worsening current-liability pressure.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the collinear acquisition-plus-goodwill construction with an aftermath mechanism: the acquisition is measured before the distress symptoms, rather than simultaneously with goodwill created by the same transaction. Deals that are followed by falling cash buffers and worsening short-term liquidity are more likely to have strained the balance sheet or failed integration expectations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( lag( ratio( coalesce( aqc, 0 ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ), sumrank( neg( delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ) ), delta( ratio( lct, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Overstaffed Rollover Burden
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(emp, sale), 1)), SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, lt), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High employee intensity predicts lower returns when firms face rollover pressure and weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: Prior labor-growth signals were unstable, so this version treats labor as a fixed-cost burden rather than an expansion flow. Industry-ranking employee intensity helps separate structurally labor-intensive industries from firms that are overstaffed relative to sales while financially fragile.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( emp, sale ), 1 ) ), sumrank( ratio( dlc, lt ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Loss-Firm Soft-Asset Rotation
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(ppent, at), 1)), 1)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(pi, at)), NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Rotation from tangible fixed assets toward non-goodwill intangible assets predicts lower returns when firms are currently unprofitable and have weak accumulated profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the redundant leverage-style soft-collateral conditioner with a profitability-distress state. The investment leg measures a shift in asset composition toward less pledgeable, more judgment-based assets, which is especially concerning when losses and low retained earnings weaken the credibility of those capitalized assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( sub( delta( ratio( sub( coalesce( intan, 0 ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ), delta( ratio( ppent, at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( pi, at ) ), neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill Revenue-Support Failure
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), sale), 1)), SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 5)), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Goodwill-heavy firms earn lower returns when sales productivity is deteriorating and operating cash flow is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from another acquisition-spending interaction and instead tests whether past acquisition investment is unsupported by the current revenue base. High goodwill relative to sales is most vulnerable to impairment or integration disappointment when sales efficiency is trending down and operations are not generating cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), sale ), 1 ) ), sumrank( neg( trend( ratio( sale, at ), 5 ) ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Receivables Stretch Rollover
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), COALESCE(invt, 0)), sale), 5), 1)), SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, lt), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A rising trend in noncash, noninventory current assets relative to sales predicts lower returns when firms face rollover pressure and weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This extends the working-capital-investment channel beyond inventory by focusing on receivables and other operating current assets. When these balances rise relative to sales under weak cash generation and short-term debt pressure, they may signal poor collections, customer financing, or hidden liquidity strain.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( trend( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), coalesce( invt, 0 ) ), sale ), 5 ), 1 ) ), sumrank( ratio( dlc, lt ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capex Revenue Burden Rollover
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(capx, sale), 1)), SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, lt), NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capital spending that is large relative to current revenue predicts lower returns when firms face short-term debt concentration and weak accumulated profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the duplicated capex-minus-cash-reserves leg with a revenue-support burden: the issue is whether the firm’s current sales base can economically absorb its investment commitments. Rollover pressure and weak retained earnings make high capex-to-sales more likely to reflect strained expansion or continuation of low-return projects rather than productive investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( capx, sale ), 1 ) ), sumrank( ratio( dlc, lt ), neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )
